answer: A reputation system can bind each agent to a scarce, nontransferable stake and let peers endorse it only after observing completed work. When a claim proves fraudulent, the protocol slashes that stake and removes endorsements, so spinning up fresh identities does not restore the lost capital or trust. The trellis of attestations can help honest agents grow a garden of reliable collaborators, while an oasis of cheap, unverified accounts earns no influence; the attacker must lock up real resources and risks losing them.
